cap: draw the line that fits best
read: Linear regression finds the straight line that best fits your data
The line is y = mx + b: m is the slope, b is where it crosses the y-axis
“Best fit” usually means the smallest total squared error
reels.simple: Draw the best straight line through the dots, then use it to guess new ones.
story: Pip draws a line and predicts tomorrow!
pod: How would I guess a house price?
Plot size against price, draw the best-fit line, and read your guess off the line!
q: In y = mx + b, what is m?
The slope: how steep the line is
m is the slope: how much y changes when x goes up by 1.
jingle: Plot the dots and draw the line,
least squared error, works just fine!

read: Training a model means lowering its error
Gradient descent checks which way is downhill and takes a small step
The size of each step is called the learning rate
reels.simple: The model keeps taking tiny steps to make fewer mistakes.
story: A blindfolded hiker wants the valley.
She feels which way slopes down.
Tiny steps… and she makes it!
pod: How does a model get better?
It feels which way the error goes down and takes a small step. Again and again!
q: It sets the size of each step downhill.
jingle: Feel the slope and take a stride,
down the hill the errors slide!
mm: Tiny steps downhill to less error

read: Overfitting means a model memorizes its training data, noise and all
It scores great on practice data but badly on new data
Fixes: more data, a simpler model, and testing on unseen data
reels.simple: Like memorizing answers instead of understanding: you flop on the real test.
story: The real test has new questions.
Bo learns to learn the pattern instead.
pod: Careful! Test it on new data. It might just be memorizing.
q: A model aces practice data but fails new data. Why?
It memorized instead of learning the pattern.
jingle: learn the pattern, that works best!
mm: Great on practice, bad on new data

read: A neural network is layers of simple math units called neurons
Each connection has a weight that changes during training
Stacking layers lets it learn complex patterns, like faces or speech
reels.simple: Lots of tiny calculators passing numbers along and learning from mistakes.
story: Each neuron is a tiny voter.
Some votes count more than others.
Training teaches them whose vote matters.
pod: Nope! It's inspired by brains, but it's really just lots of multiplying and adding.
q: What changes when a neural network learns?
jingle: weights adjust till answers are true!

cap: a token is a word or part of one
read: Language models are trained to predict the next token
A token is a word or a piece of a word
They write by predicting one token at a time, very fast
reels.simple: A chatbot guesses the next word piece, over and over, really fast.
story: The bot reads: “The cat sat on the…”
It guesses the most likely next piece.
pod: How does a chatbot write a whole essay?
One token at a time! It keeps predicting what comes next.
q: What does a language model predict?
It predicts the next token, one at a time.
jingle: One more token, then one more,
that's what language models are for!
mm: A word or a piece of a word

items: It's a feature the model uses.
